decisions.audience: Personal setup first, then invited streamers
decisions.unattended: First release must prove Twitch event -> OBS alert through a local background worker while chat is closed

milestones.title: M1 — Personal streaming and unattended alerts
milestones.description: Twitch account/channel update, independent OBS and Stream Deck, and a real event-to-OBS alert while chat is closed.

milestones.title: M2 — Invited streamers and creative workflows
milestones.description: Optional creative/media integrations, native extension improvements, and verified invited-user onboarding/access.

milestones.title: M3 — Analytics recipe catalog and distribution
milestones.description: Named analytics datasets, broader reusable recipes, and public submission readiness.

tracks.name: Core and recipes
tracks.goal: Publish small shared interfaces and run reviewed recipes without coupling provider implementations.

tracks.name: Twitch accounts and API
tracks.goal: Connect the creator account and expose scoped Twitch reads and reviewed channel updates.

tracks.name: OBS
tracks.goal: Inspect and change isolated OBS resources through an optional local provider.

tracks.name: Stream Deck
tracks.goal: Inspect the local deck and preview/apply a dedicated test profile without Twitch dependency.

tracks.name: Events and background automation
tracks.goal: Receive Twitch events and trigger an OBS alert from a resident local worker while chat is closed.

tracks.name: Clips game data and analytics
tracks.goal: Acquire authorized clips, enrich game/media metadata, and expose named analytics datasets.

tracks.name: Creative tools
tracks.goal: Coordinate existing design connections and produce portable assets without vendoring full products.

tracks.name: Native UI and onboarding
tracks.goal: Verify native plugin behavior and guide users through optional integrations with host-capability fallbacks.

tracks.name: Release and distribution
tracks.goal: Prove personal dogfood first, then isolate invited-user accounts and prepare wider distribution.

items.title: Define versioned capability, account, event, asset, and recipe interfaces
items.scope: Own only src/contracts/ and shared contract fixtures. Publish a minimal interface version first so independent adapters can compile against it.
accept: Define provider and account references, execution location, required grants, mock/live provenance, action plans, event envelopes, asset references, and normalized errors.
Provide fixtures for success, missing connection/grant, invalid input, stale state, rate limits, cancellation, and unavailable providers.
Recipes name capabilities rather than arbitrary upstream tool names. Provider adapters can be developed without starting another provider.
Record a short interface-change process; contract changes do not silently break another track.

items.title: Resolve capabilities across optional MCP servers and connected plugins
items.scope: Own src/providers/. Resolve known adapters and host-coordinated plugin capabilities without assuming backend access to every installed plugin.
accept: Distinguish installed, connected, authorized, available, and verified states.
Select one canonical provider per capability with deterministic fallback rules and provenance.
A disconnected Twitch account does not disable OBS, Stream Deck, public metadata, or design-only recipes.
No arbitrary tool forwarding, invented app IDs, credential copying, or automatic startup of unreviewed servers.

items.title: Load reusable recipes and generate target-bound action previews
items.scope: Own src/recipes/schema/ and src/recipes/planner/. Migrate prepare-channel and add an OBS or deck fixture recipe.
accept: Version recipe definitions and input schemas; validate target, capability requirements, and mock/live mode.
Preview returns exact before/after values, effects, expiry, and immutable input/version references without calling mutation adapters.
Chat and UI consume the same plan. Unknown recipes, wrong targets, unavailable capabilities, and stale plans have explicit errors.
Fixture tests run without real accounts or devices.

items.title: Execute approved recipes with durable runs and idempotent steps
items.scope: Own src/recipes/executor/ and run-store interfaces. Accept interactive approval or an explicit unattended grant; never infer authorization from a preview.
accept: Recheck account/device ownership, plan expiry, recipe version, and permissions at execution.
Persist step outcomes, cancellation, failure, and artifact references; reconcile ambiguous writes rather than retrying blindly.
Reject mock plans at live adapters. Duplicate invocation keys do not repeat side effects.
Define provider-independent storage and fake-clock tests; local implementation does not claim multi-user hosting.

items.title: Connect a Twitch account and manage grants and token lifecycle
items.scope: Own src/auth/ and Twitch credential adapters. Reuse selected Stream Makeover OAuth logic after removing Sites-specific owner/storage coupling. Start design and regression-test extraction now.
accept: Record the supported local authorization path, callback registration, credential-store choice, and one-account personal-dogfood ownership model; keep IDs extensible for later accounts.
Connect, validate at startup/hourly, refresh, reconnect, and disconnect. Serialize refresh and handle revocation.
Regression tests cover replay/expired state, wrong owner, missing scope, refresh rotation, and disconnect races.
Use fnox/1Password for developer secrets; never return/log credentials. Verify real connection separately from browser/host sign-in.

items.title: Add the minimal read-only Twitch channel and category tools
items.scope: Own src/adapters/twitch/reads/. Review twitch-mcp-server as a source/reference and pin any adopted dependency.
accept: Support account/profile reads, channel details, and category lookup with pagination and rate-limit errors. Clip, video, and chat metadata are separate later work.
Public app-token reads do not require streamer OAuth. User-scoped reads integrate with the account grant interface.
Verify one harmless real query before broader checks. Exclude undocumented GraphQL comments from the supported contract.
Record provider version/license notices; MCP read annotations match behavior.

items.title: Preview and apply a reviewed Twitch channel update
items.scope: Own src/adapters/twitch/channel/ and recipes/twitch/prepare-channel. Fixture implementation can start before real OAuth.
accept: Preview exact account, title, category, and selected supported fields; recheck channel:manage:broadcast and token/broadcaster identity.
Execute only the approved unexpired plan, then read back values.
Reject substituted targets, missing grants, changed inputs, and mock plans. Reconcile ambiguous failures.
Document which obs-twitch-mcp handlers are references only; do not start its chat/moderation services.

items.title: Select the OBS provider and implement read-only preflight
items.scope: Own src/adapters/obs/discovery/. Compare agentic-obs and obs-twitch-mcp, selecting one canonical provider per required capability. No Twitch OAuth dependency.
accept: Record pinned source, actual discovered tools, license/runtime requirements, and supported status/scene/source/audio reads.
Distinguish missing MCP server, unreachable OBS, and unsupported action.
Check the running obs-studio-rust instance through localhost:4455 for this setup; never launch a second OBS instance or change server authentication.
No broadcast/recording change, group-enabling call, or chat startup occurs during preflight. Start with one read-only query.

items.title: Audit and isolate useful obs-twitch-mcp capabilities before adoption
items.scope: Review source and compare gaps with the chosen OBS provider. Implement an OBS-only upstream fork mode only if the comparison finds a needed capability.
accept: Source review identifies startup chat/spam bans, token output/storage, dependencies, and unresolved redistribution notices.
If adopted, tests prove OBS-only startup does not instantiate Twitch/chat/moderation or unrelated background automations and works without Twitch credentials.
Keep duplicated capabilities out of the installed configuration. Record a pinned fork revision and upstream issue/PR for any changes.
A documented decision not to adopt is a valid result when another provider covers the need.

items.title: Preview and verify isolated OBS source changes and alert output
items.scope: Own src/adapters/obs/actions/ and recipes/obs/. Provide a narrow text/browser-source alert action used by the background workflow.
accept: Show exact source/scene target, before/after settings, and cleanup/rollback behavior.
Allow writes only to explicitly selected test resources; preserve broadcast, recording, program scene, and unrelated sources.
Verify one isolated source update and restore it. If this OBS variant cannot render the isolated scene, record the limitation and define an explicit test procedure before program changes.
Expose a constrained alert-display capability for automation; no generic arbitrary OBS command or script execution.

items.title: Discover Stream Deck devices profiles and reusable actions
items.scope: Own src/adapters/streamdeck/discovery/. Use the profile-writer provider independently of Twitch; treat USB mode as a separate choice.
accept: Inventory selected device geometry, profiles/pages, buttons/dials, and configured actions; multiple-device fixtures require explicit selection.
Distinguish unavailable server, absent device, protected plugin metadata, and unsupported platform.
No profile write, app restart, script creation, or USB ownership change during discovery.
Verify one harmless inventory query on the user's device; pin the intended fork rather than an upstream package with the same identity.

items.title: Preview a Stream Deck page from configured actions
items.scope: Own recipes/streamdeck/ and page-plan schema. Optional OBS scene names can be supplied by fixtures.
accept: Show exact button/dial placement, source action IDs, geometry validation, and unsupported controls.
Prefer existing configured actions. Preview emits declarative data without scripts or profile writes.
Layout-only preview works without Twitch or OBS; an OBS-specific action is unavailable only when its own capability is missing.
Tests preserve opaque provider settings when copying configured actions.

items.title: Apply and restore one dedicated Stream Deck test profile
items.scope: Own src/adapters/streamdeck/actions/. Begin with a scratch profile tree before touching hardware.
accept: Validate target paths and restrict writes to a dedicated test profile copy. Never overwrite the active profile.
Preview identifies any Elgato app quit/restart requirement before execution.
Back up the test profile manifest, write one page, verify on real hardware, and prove restore.
Preserve configured action settings and reject arbitrary generated shell scripts.

items.title: Manage EventSub subscription intent and connection lifecycle
items.scope: Own src/events/subscriptions/. First personal release uses a local WebSocket receiver in the background worker; shared event/subscription interfaces avoid a circular dependency with delivery.
accept: Create/list/delete/reconcile desired subscriptions, event type/version/condition, owner, and observed enabled state.
Enforce event-specific scopes and user-token identity for WebSockets; select a first testable event during implementation.
Handle duplicate intents, revocation, reconnect/session replacement, and unsubscribe.

Requested subscription is never reported as enabled without Twitch evidence. Component acceptance uses fake session tests; real create/enable and receipt are verified by the integrated event-to-OBS issue.

items.title: Receive normalize and deduplicate EventSub WebSocket events
items.scope: Own src/events/receiver/. Use fixture sessions/events independently of real OAuth and the subscription manager.
accept: Handle welcome, keepalive, server-directed reconnect, and unexpected disconnect; expose gaps instead of promising replay.
Normalize provider event/subscription IDs, account, timestamp, type, and payload; durably record accepted events and processing state.
Duplicate receipts do not repeat recipe effects. Bounded retries and failed-event inspection are explicit.
Component acceptance uses fixture sessions and durable handoff tests. The integrated event-to-OBS issue owns real subscription, receiver, and worker acceptance.

items.title: Run a local background worker independently of chat
items.scope: Own src/worker/ lifecycle and local runtime storage. No hosted service or cloud-to-desktop bridge is required for this personal release.
accept: User can start, stop, inspect, and restart the worker explicitly. Only one worker owns each local event session.
Worker survives chat closure and reports process/offline state, health, run history, and reconnect status.
Persist accepted events/runs across worker restarts; redact credentials and document OS startup behavior without silently enabling startup.
Provide fake-event and fake-adapter modes so development does not require Twitch or OBS. Desktop sleep/offline limitations are explicit.
The worker owns its own vetted MCP client or direct OBS connection, including startup/reconnect, credential references, and cleanup. It does not depend on a chat host exposing installed plugin tools.

items.title: Authorize bounded unattended recipes and support pause and revocation
items.scope: Own src/worker/policy/. An unattended authorization binds a recipe version, event/account, allowed actions, target, duration, and rate limits.
accept: Preview and explicit activation create a durable grant; a chat suggestion alone cannot authorize execution.
Enforce target allowlists, expiry, revocation, duplicate-event keys, cooldown/backpressure, and maximum queued actions.
Pause, disconnect, or revoked credentials prevent subsequent effects. Test crashes, retries, offline devices, and cancellation with fake clocks.
No unrestricted broadcast controls, profile writes, or arbitrary tool forwarding in the first alert recipe.

items.title: Prove a Twitch event triggers an OBS alert while chat is closed
items.scope: Own recipes/alerts/twitch-obs/ and tests/integration/event-obs/. This is the required unattended acceptance test for the first release.
accept: Authorize one concrete event→alert recipe for the creator account and a dedicated OBS test resource.
Close chat, deliver a real subscribed Twitch event, and verify the visible OBS alert plus a correlated durable run record.
Replay a duplicate fixture and prove no duplicate alert; restart worker and verify recovery, then pause/revoke and prove later events cannot trigger effects.
Preserve broadcast/program state and remove only test resources. Record local-worker uptime requirements and unsupported offline replay.
Verify that the worker's independently owned OBS connection still functions after the chat host disconnects.

items.title: Download an authorized Twitch clip through the official API
items.scope: Own src/adapters/twitch/clips/ and asset-storage adapters. Listing clips is distinct from downloading media.
accept: Request authorized official download URLs with the required broadcaster/editor grant; handle expiry and nullable formats.
Download one authorized clip first, then cover batch/rate limits, interrupted transfer, cancellation, and renewal.
Return asset ID, source clip/channel, size, checksum, media type, and provenance without credentials.
Use obs-twitch-mcp only as a reviewed handler/workflow reference; do not adopt its startup/auth behavior.

items.title: Add optional media metadata transcripts and search
items.scope: Own src/adapters/media/. Adapt the selected yt-media-info-mcp fork; no Twitch account or clip downloader required for public URLs.
accept: Verify frontend/backend readiness separately and normalize metadata/transcript/search results with provenance.
Keep the Python backend private and use secret references for optional credentials; no exposed unauthenticated cookie service.
Missing transcripts and unavailable provider return explicit results and do not disable unrelated recipes.
Advertise no media-download capability; verify one public record before broader calls.

items.title: Resolve IGDB game metadata and Twitch category mappings
items.scope: Own src/adapters/igdb/. Choose the supplied Pipeworx relay or a direct IGDB adapter using the developer application after documenting routing/auth tradeoffs.
accept: Record the mcp-igdb relay dependency, its credentials, rate limits, and data destination before enabling it.
Return game metadata and asset provenance; keep IGDB IDs distinct from Twitch category IDs and map via Twitch igdb_id.
Verify one game lookup and missing-provider behavior; no streamer OAuth or EventSub dependency.
Pin the provider/version or document the direct adapter decision.

items.title: Expose named analytics datasets with source and coverage
items.scope: Own src/analytics/. Define API snapshots, event-derived metrics, imported reports, and eligible developer game/extension reports as distinct datasets.
accept: Every result includes source, period, timezone, freshness, collection start, and gaps.
Do not claim full Creator Dashboard historical analytics or equate estimates with authoritative viewer data.
Implement fixture/import aggregation first. Snapshot acceptance integrates with Helix; event-derived datasets integrate with delivery; developer reports require applicable scope/ownership.
Tests cover duplicate events, missing intervals, timezone boundaries, and unavailable metrics.

items.title: Coordinate the existing OpenDesign Cloud plugin and MCP connection
items.scope: Own src/adapters/design/opendesign/ and one recipe skill. Preserve the user's existing deployment/authentication; do not copy its daemon.
accept: Discover actual deployed tools, connection status, run lifecycle, and artifact references; source repo does not prove remote transport/auth.
Use a fixture brief first, then create one isolated test project through the verified connection and return an asset reference.
Handle cancellation, provider failure, and missing connection. No invented app ID or duplicate deployment.
Keep host-driven plugin coordination distinct from backend adapter permissions.

items.title: Render one portable HyperFrames alert overlay
items.scope: Own src/adapters/hyperframes/ and one overlay template. Reuse the existing portable HTML approach; no OBS or OpenDesign runtime required for authoring.
accept: Use a pinned CLI/provider and fixture variables to render one alert asset; verify dimensions, decoded motion/alpha where relevant, and cleanup.
Output runs in a stock browser and stock OBS without experimental flags, authoring CLI, or secrets.
Return an asset reference that OBS can consume later. Keep template assets and licenses traceable.
Discover whether an appropriate plugin exists before adding a new dependency; do not invent a HyperFrames endpoint.

items.title: Add optional Canva artwork workflow through its existing plugin
items.scope: Own src/adapters/design/canva/ and one artwork recipe. No bundling of Canva or copied account credentials.
accept: Discover actual connection and supported operations; use verified provider identifiers.
Preview one thumbnail or stream schedule brief using fixtures, then create one isolated test design if the connection supports it.
Return design/export references and handle missing capabilities; no automatic publishing or spending beyond authorized operations.
Missing Canva disables only Canva-specific execution.

items.title: Verify the installed Stream Machine plugin in the native host
items.scope: Own docs/verification/native/ and host integration checks. Existing installation is a starting point, not proof of native rendering.
accept: Record installed version/source, actual stdio tool discovery, harmless call, MCP App resource rendering, global/thread entrypoints, and onboarding invocation.
Verify reset/restart behavior and distinguish browser preview from native-host evidence.
Report desktop, Work web, classic ChatGPT, iOS, and Android capability limits accurately; do not claim localhost access from mobile.
Document defects as targeted follow-up issues without recreating the plugin or breaking current connections.

items.title: Make onboarding resumable and provider-aware
items.scope: Own skills/onboarding/ and setup UI. Use connection-state fixtures before real integrations exist.
accept: Discover existing plugins first; distinguish installed, connected, authorized, and verified. Support skip/resume and optional provider setup.
Separate demo reset from real provider disconnect. Request only scopes needed for selected recipes.
Route Twitch, OBS, and Stream Deck setup independently; unsupported platform tools stay clearly unavailable.
First-run completion includes a harmless real check for each selected provider and an explicit separate activation step for unattended automation.

items.title: Add native settings mentions deep links and context fallbacks
items.scope: Own src/ui/extensions/. Use standard MCP Apps first and feature-detect each OpenAI Extension.
accept: Implement settings for selected account/device/default recipe, composer resource search, validated recipe/run deep links, and selected context where the host supports them.
Provide chat tools or in-app pickers for unsupported hosts; keep state ownership and authoritative server updates clear.
Test theme/safe areas and narrow/tablet/desktop sizes; do not label Work web support as classic ChatGPT parity.
Evaluate a recipe/artifact file handler only for supported hosts and authorized file access. Document unavailable features rather than simulating support.

items.title: Verify and package the first personal release
items.scope: Own docs/releases/personal/ and release integration tests. Coordinate the owner of root manifests/build files so provider branches do not conflict.
accept: Demonstrate account connection and reviewed channel update, standalone OBS preflight/action, standalone Stream Deck test profile, and real event→OBS alert while chat is closed.
Verify account/device boundaries, revocation, worker pause/restart, rollback, and secret redaction; keep broadcasts and active profiles unchanged during QA.
Install/update the built package through the supported host workflow, verify tool/UI discovery, and record exact dependency versions and notices.
Document that desktop/worker availability limits unattended behavior. M1 does not claim hosted or mobile execution of local tools.

items.title: Decide and implement invited-user identity and hosted MCP access
items.scope: Own deployment/ and hosted identity/storage adapters. Architecture research can start now; implementation needs a recorded stack/ownership decision. This implementation proceeds only if the invited-access decision selects hosted MCP; otherwise document that the capability remains deferred without blocking local invited setups.
accept: Decide account multiplicity, invited-user isolation, credential storage, callback domains, data retention, and hosting based on tested requirements.
Expose authenticated remote MCP with tenant/account authorization if hosted access is selected; isolate desktop credentials and local tools.
Test wrong-user access, reconnect/revocation, token redaction, and cross-device state. Keep Sites identity/auth separate from Twitch grants.
Choose hosting only after comparing supported runtimes and native extension behavior. No generic cloud-to-desktop bridge in scope without a concrete requirement.

items.title: Validate installation onboarding and upgrades with invited streamers
items.scope: Own docs/releases/invited/ and compatibility checks. Hosted implementation is a completion gate only if the accepted access-model decision includes hosted clients. Advanced Extensions are optional, not a blanket beta prerequisite.
accept: Validate a clean-machine installation, optional provider skip/resume, supported desktop setup, and hosted views where available.
Confirm independent account/device ownership and inability to access another streamer's credentials or resources.
Exercise upgrades, disconnect/uninstall cleanup, missing provider versions, and clear unsupported-platform messages.
Record feedback and defects per integration rather than treating one successful setup as universal compatibility.

items.title: Prepare public plugin submission and reusable recipe catalog
items.scope: Own public submission docs and recipe catalog review. Public upload is a separate release action, not part of board setup. Optional provider issues block only recipes included in the selected public release; the entire optional catalog is not a prerequisite.
accept: Review provider licenses/notices, privacy/data routing, credentials, listing claims, onboarding, permissions, and platform limitations.
Publish versioned recipe docs with inputs, dependencies, preview behavior, unattended policy, recovery, and actual verification status.
Prepare a supported upload copy with verified endpoints/app dependencies per the target distribution rules; never bundle invented connections.
Record a submission checklist and concrete install/use examples. Public release proceeds only after its separate approval/release task.

items.title: Extend Twitch read tools to streams clips videos and chat metadata
items.scope: Own src/adapters/twitch/reads/extended/. Work independently from the minimal M1 channel lookup module.
accept: Add selected stream, clip/video listing, chat settings/assets, and search reads behind explicit capabilities.
Handle provider pagination, timestamp normalization, rate limits, and per-endpoint token/scope requirements.
Exclude undocumented archived-comments GraphQL. Do not imply that clip listing downloads media.
Verify one harmless record, then use fixtures for broader coverage. Missing optional reads do not block M1 channel updates.

items.title: Choose invited-user access account ownership and hosting scope
items.scope: Record the access decision before hosted implementation. Independent local installations are a valid invited release; mobile/web access is a separate requirement.
accept: Decide whether invited users need local desktop packages, a shared authenticated hosted core, or both.
Decide account multiplicity/team ownership, credential storage/retention, and data isolation requirements with the user.
Evaluate supported hosting/runtime/authentication options only if hosted access is selected; do not silently reuse Sites identity as Twitch authorization.
List exact required platform features and conditional release gates. Advanced native extensions and hosted access are not automatic prerequisites for local beta.
